newsitem.title: UK: Europe shares steady to firmer after Wall St drop.
newsitem.headline: Europe shares steady to firmer after Wall St drop.

text.p: European shares opened steady to firmer on Thursday after Wednesday's hefty losses on Wall Street, with prices underpinned by steady bond markets, dealers said.

The FTSE 100 index, which dropped 53 points on Wednesday, opened 5.3 points higher at 3,987.0. Trading volume was a meagre 15 million shares by the open, reflecting nervousness over a possible sharp correction for U.S. shares, dealers said.
"A lot of people believe the Dow is headed south (lower)," one senior trader said.
But dealers did not expect any panic selling. "Market makers will lower prices a bit and see if they can find any buyers. But it's all guess work until Wall Street opens," onne said.
The Dow industrials average ended Wednesday's session down 70.73 points at 6,402.52.
German shares appeared to shrug off Wall Street's weak close and climbed in early Frankfurt trading but traders were not certain the gains would last through the session.
In early trade, the German 30-share IBIS DAX index was up 14.33 points at 2,850.28 in electronic pre-bourse trading, after having tested the 2,856.44 point level.
French stocks were also expected to open higher.
Dutch shares opened easier on Thursday, drifting from Wednesday's sharply lower closing and finding little support from steady bonds and the dollar.
Other European bourses were also mostly seen steady to firmer.
Markets across Asia took a nosedive on Thursday, with Tokyo falling more than 100 points in early trade and Hong Kong dropping sharply.
